title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these notes belong to the 'équation des lacets' manuscripts (sequel to La Longue Marche, c. 1981). Grothendieck is studying automorphisms u of the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, and of its extension by the symmetries ρ (order 3) and τ_∞ (orientation-reversing). These automorphisms are written in the form 'Galois-type twist φ̂ composed with an inner twist by α', and he is deriving the analogue of the order-3 (pentagon/hexagon-type) relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

What the previous page established:
- u(ρ) = ρ^μ with μ ≡ ±1 mod 3.
- Set α_3 ∈ Z/2 by (−1)^{α_3} ≡ μ mod 3. Then u(ρ) = τ'_∞^{α_3}(ρ).
- The condition coming from x = l_∞ in (5) becomes: τ'_∞^{α_3} φ̂(f_∞) α commutes with ρ, inside Ŝ_{0,3} = Ŝ^+_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞}.

Step 1 (this page). He invokes 'general principles', admitting they are not all established in the profinite setting. The principle is that the centralizer of the torsion element ρ in this 'quantisation group' is just ⟨ρ⟩ = {1, ρ, ρ²}. Hence τ'_∞^{α_3} φ̂(f_∞) α = ρ^j for a uniquely determined j ∈ Z/3. The margin note says explicit formulas 'should be given'.

Step 2: compute f_∞.
- Here f_0 = f_1 = 1 and g = ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1}.
- So f_∞^{-1} = g ρ(g) ρ²(f_0^{-1}) = g ρ(g).
- Since ρ³ = 1, the product telescopes: g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = α ρ³(α)^{-1} = 1.
- Hence g ρ(g) = ρ²(g)^{-1} = ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}), i.e. f_∞ = ρ^{-1}(ξ).

Step 3: solve for φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ)).
- From Step 1, φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ)) = τ'^{α_3} ρ^j α^{-1}, using that τ' is an involution.
- Rewrite τ'^{α_3} ρ^j = τ'^{α_3}(ρ^j) τ'^{α_3}.
- Since τ'_∞(ρ) = ρ^{-1}, we get τ'^{α_3}(ρ^j) = ρ^{j'} with j' = (−1)^{α_3} j.
- Result (44): φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ)) = ρ^{j'} τ'_∞^{α_3} α^{-1}.

Step 4: normalise.
- Write τ'_∞^{α_3} = (σ_∞ τ_∞)^{α_3} = σ_∞^{α_3} τ_∞^{α_3}; this is legitimate because α_3 ∈ {0,1}.
- Then τ'^{α_3} α^{-1} = σ_∞^{α_3} (α τ_∞^{α_3})^{-1} = σ_∞^{α_3} α̃^{-1}.
- On the next page, α̃ = α τ_∞^{α_3} is shown to lie in π̂_{0,3} in all cases. This leads to the boxed formula (47)/(48), which expresses α̃ in terms of φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1})), ρ^{j'} and σ_∞^{α_3}.

Purpose: obtain an explicit 'order-3' normal form for the twisting cocycle. This is the analogue of the relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1 in the definition of GT. Here the case λ ≡ −1 mod 3 is handled by composing with the orientation-reversing element τ'_∞ rather than excluded.
errors: The struck intermediate line writes τ'_∞ ρ^j α^{-1} without the exponent α_3; Grothendieck's correction above it supplies τ'^{α_3}(ρ^j) τ'^{α_3}. The final formula (44) is correct.

The key step (the centralizer of ρ is ⟨ρ⟩ in the profinite group) is explicitly flagged as not established in the profinite setting. It is a gap at the time of writing, later filled by results on centralizers of torsion in profinite free products (Herfort–Ribes).
Equation number (44) is reused: it already labels the commutation condition on the previous page.

ideas.what: The centralizer of the order-3 torsion element ρ in the profinite (extended) group π̂_{0,3}⋊(symmetries) is exactly ⟨ρ⟩, used to turn a commutation condition into an equation '= ρ^j'.
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of torsion elements / finite subgroups in profinite free products (e.g. the profinite completion of PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 ∗ Z/3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes (mid-1980s), Ribes–Zalesskii; used in Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak–Schneps treatments of ĜT

ideas.what: Telescoping identity: for ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} with ρ³ = 1, one has ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, hence f_∞ = ρ^{-1}(ξ).
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary / cocycle identity for a Z/3-action

ideas.what: Deriving the order-3 relation of the Teichmüller-type group in the presence of orientation reversal: the parity α_3 encodes λ mod 3 (λ ≡ ±1), absorbed by τ'_∞ = σ_∞ τ_∞.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon / order-3 relation of ĜT; extended GT including complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Grothendieck's Esquisse for the programme

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that the centralizer result for torsion elements in the profinite setting is 'not all established' and wants explicit formulas. This is an early recognition of a profinite group-theoretic input later supplied independently.
missed.quote: d'après les principes généraux (pas tous établis, à vrai dire, dans le cadre profini) le commutateur de ρ dans le groupe de quantisation est réduit au groupe engendré par ρ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck isolated the needed profinite centralizer lemma for the GT order-3 relation before Herfort–Ribes and before Drinfeld's GT. It is not new mathematics today.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine computational step in Grothendieck's own derivation of a GT-type order-3 relation. The only noteworthy point is his explicit awareness that the profinite centralizer lemma was unproved; it was later proved and is now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'le commutateur de ρ' is presumably meant as 'le commutant (centralisateur) de ρ'.
'la relation α_3[?]' is likely 'la relation (44)' or 'la relation α'.
The struck line 'τ'_∞ ρ^j α^{-1}' should read τ'_∞^{α_3} ρ^j α^{-1}; Grothendieck's added correction is τ'^{α_3}_∞(ρ^j) τ'^{α_3}_∞.
'facto[?]' at the top is probably 'ipso facto' or part of the margin note; the margin reads roughly 'il faudrait en donner des formules explicites, précises, presque!!!!'.
